questions.title: What makes a method recursive?
questions.description: Which description best identifies a recursive method?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.

options.text: It calls itself directly or indirectly
It always uses a for loop

hints: Look for a call path that returns to the same method.
questions.explanation: It calls itself directly or through another method.

questions.title: Factorial base case
questions.description: For factorial(n), where n is a nonnegative integer, which base result stops recursion correctly?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Choose the smallest valid input whose answer is known.
questions.explanation: By definition, 0! equals 1, so that input can return without another call.

questions.title: Count down result
questions.description: What does countDown(3) print if it prints n, then calls countDown(n - 1) while n > 0?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Trace each call until the stopping condition.
questions.explanation: The method prints the current value before the smaller call.

questions.title: Recursive sum of one
questions.description: A method returns 0 for n == 0; otherwise it returns n + sum(n - 1). What is sum(1)?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Expand just one call.
questions.explanation: The recursive step adds 1 to the base result 0.

questions.title: Sum from zero through n
questions.description: Fill the missing recursive argument: return n + sumTo(___); the base case is n == 0.
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Decrease the argument by one.
questions.explanation: The next call must move one step closer to zero.

questions.title: Trace recursive product
questions.description: A product(n) method returns 1 at n == 1, otherwise n * product(n - 1). What is product(4)?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Write the call chain down to the base case.
questions.explanation: The calls multiply 4 × 3 × 2 × 1.

questions.title: Identify the recursive step
questions.description: A recursive power method handles exponent 0 and computes base * power(base, exponent - 1). Which part is the recursive step?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: The base case returns without calling the method.
questions.explanation: The multiplication followed by the call with a smaller exponent makes progress.

questions.title: Recursive triangular number
questions.description: Define tri(0)=0 and tri(n)=n+tri(n-1). What is tri(5)?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Accumulate each value while descending.
questions.explanation: The result is 5+4+3+2+1+0.

questions.title: Call count for a linear recursion
questions.description: A method makes one call with n-1 until n reaches 0. Starting at n=6, how many total invocations occur, including the initial call and base call?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Count the base invocation too.
questions.explanation: Calls occur for 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, and 0.

questions.title: When direct recursion fails to progress
questions.description: A method has base case n == 0, but for positive n it calls solve(n). What is the main defect?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.

options.text: The recursive call makes no progress toward the base case
The method has too many parameters
Every recursive method must use two calls
The base case should always return n

hints: Compare the recursive argument with the stopping condition.
questions.explanation: The argument never approaches zero, so the base case is unreachable for positive input.

questions.title: Empty range base case
questions.description: A method processes indices from left to right using index i. Which condition naturally ends when the array is exhausted?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Valid indices stop at length - 1.
questions.explanation: When i reaches the array length, there is no element left to process.

questions.title: Stack frames unwind
questions.description: A method prints enter; if n > 0 it calls itself with n-1; then it prints exit. What is output for n=1?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Separate work before and after the recursive call.
questions.explanation: The second call reaches its base behavior before either frame prints exit.

questions.title: Base case for countdown
questions.description: Complete the condition that stops a countdown for all n <= 0: if (n ___ 0) return;
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Use the comparison that includes equality and smaller values.
questions.explanation: The stop condition includes zero and negative values.

questions.title: Stack depth
questions.description: A recursive method makes one call for each integer from 4 down to 0. What is its maximum number of simultaneously active frames?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Count the inclusive sequence.
questions.explanation: All five calls are active before the deepest frame returns.

questions.title: Find the missing base return
questions.description: A boolean recursive search checks one item then advances. Which base return is appropriate when index == array.length?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: The success case returns true at the matching item.
questions.explanation: Once every element has been checked without a match, the search should report false.

questions.title: Output after recursive call
questions.description: For n>0, method f prints n after calling f(n-1), and returns at n==0. What is printed by f(3)?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Follow the return order.
questions.explanation: Printing after the call happens during unwinding, from the smallest positive frame upward.

questions.title: Avoiding a missing base case
questions.description: A recursive method handles n>0 but has no branch for n<=0. What risk does calling it with 0 create?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.

options.text: Non-terminating recursion and eventual stack overflow

hints: Check whether every valid input path returns or stops.
questions.explanation: It can repeatedly call itself without reaching a terminating return.

questions.title: Correct recursive descent
questions.description: For a method that must reach base case n == 1 from n > 1, fill in the argument: solve(___).
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Use the predecessor.
questions.explanation: The argument must strictly decrease toward one.

questions.title: Two-branch call count
questions.description: calls(n) returns at n==0; otherwise it calls calls(n-1) twice. How many invocations occur for calls(2), including the first call?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Count the repeated subtrees separately.

questions.title: Exception-safe stack reasoning
questions.description: A recursive parser opens a resource before recursing and closes it only after return. Which concern matters for deep input?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.

options.text: A stack overflow may interrupt normal unwind and skip cleanup
The base case is evaluated after cleanup
The resource is duplicated by the JVM

hints: Consider what happens if the deepest call fails.
questions.explanation: Deep recursion can exhaust the call stack before unwinding reaches the close operation.

questions.title: Sum an array recursively
questions.description: sum(a,i) returns 0 when i == a.length; otherwise it returns a[i] + sum(a,i+1). For a=[2,5,1], what is sum(a,0)?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Expand until i reaches 3.
questions.explanation: Each element contributes once before the empty suffix returns zero.

questions.title: Reverse string base case
questions.description: A recursive string reversal swaps characters at left and right, then moves inward. When should it stop?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: No swap is needed for an interval of length zero or one.
questions.explanation: When pointers meet or cross, all needed swaps are complete.

questions.title: Find the last element recursively
questions.description: last(a,i) returns a[i] at the final index; otherwise it calls last(a,i+1). What does last([4,7,9],0) return?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Trace indices 0, 1, then 2.
questions.explanation: The index advances until it reaches the final valid position.

questions.title: String prefix recursion
questions.description: A method counts characters recursively. To process the next character after index i, call count(text, ___).
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Advance by one.
questions.explanation: The next character is at the following index.

questions.title: Recursive maximum
questions.description: max(a,i) returns a[i] at the final index; otherwise returns max(a[i], max(a,i+1)). For [3,8,2,6], what is the result from i=0?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Reduce from the final element toward the first.
questions.explanation: The nested comparisons retain the greatest value in the suffix.

questions.title: Count matching values
questions.description: A recursive count returns 0 at the end. Fill the contribution when a[i] equals target: (a[i] == target ? ___ : 0) + count(a,i+1).
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: The contribution is a count, not the matched value.
questions.explanation: A match contributes one occurrence.

questions.title: Palindrome recursion
questions.description: For a recursive palindrome check, after equal end characters are confirmed, what smaller subproblem should be checked?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Both boundaries move inward together.
questions.explanation: Removing both equal outer characters leaves the inner substring.

questions.title: Binary search recursive range
questions.description: In recursive binary search with inclusive bounds, when mid is too small, the next lower bound is ___.
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: The next candidate begins immediately after mid.
questions.explanation: Discard mid and everything to its left.

questions.title: Recursive merge sort space
questions.description: A standard recursive merge sort uses a temporary array during merging. What is its auxiliary space complexity?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: The temporary array dominates the stack.
questions.explanation: Temporary merge storage is linear; recursion adds logarithmic stack space.

questions.title: Skip adjacent duplicates recursively
questions.description: A sorted array scan counts the first value, then adds one whenever a[i] differs from a[i-1]. For [1,1,2,2,2,4], how many distinct values are counted?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Count transitions plus the first element.
questions.explanation: The first value counts once, then changes to 2 and 4 add two more.

questions.title: Divide and conquer shape
questions.description: Which sequence best describes divide and conquer?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.

options.text: repeat the same full input forever

hints: Look for splitting plus combining.
questions.explanation: A problem is split into smaller instances, their results are combined, and a base case handles small instances.

questions.title: Binary search midpoint
questions.description: For low and high inclusive, fill a safe midpoint expression: low + (high - low) / ___.
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Use the number of halves.
questions.explanation: Integer division by two finds the middle offset.

questions.title: Merge sort base case
questions.description: A merge sort call works on indices left through right. Which range is already sorted without further splitting?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: A singleton is trivially ordered.
questions.explanation: A range with zero or one element needs no sorting.

questions.title: Sum split halves
questions.description: A recursive method splits [1,2,3,4] into halves, sums each, then adds them. What total is returned?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: The split does not change the included values.
questions.explanation: Combining the partial sums gives the original array sum.

questions.title: Binary search call depth
questions.description: A balanced binary search reduces 64 candidates by half each call. How many halvings reach one candidate?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Solve 64 / 2^k = 1.
questions.explanation: Six halvings take 64 to 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, then 1.

questions.title: Combine inversion counts
questions.description: A divide-and-conquer inversion counter sorts each half recursively. Where are cross-half inversions counted?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: The halves are individually sorted at that point.
questions.explanation: During merge, a right value placed before remaining left values forms cross inversions.

questions.title: Quicksort partition recursion
questions.description: A partition step places a pivot at index p. Which ranges are recursively sorted next, excluding the pivot?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Do not include p in either recursive range.
questions.explanation: The pivot is settled; only ranges on either side remain.

questions.title: Merge two sorted arrays logic
questions.description: While merging, if left[i] <= right[j], copy left[i] and advance ___.
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Advance the pointer whose item was consumed.
questions.explanation: The chosen item came from the left sequence.

questions.title: Recurrence for merge sort
questions.description: Which recurrence models merge sort with two half-size calls and linear merging?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Account for both halves and the merge scan.
questions.explanation: There are two subproblems of size n/2 plus linear combine work.

questions.title: Binary search off-by-one
questions.description: An inclusive binary search recurses right with low = mid. When low < high and mid rounds down, what bug can occur?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.

options.text: The range may not shrink, so recursion can repeat forever

hints: The midpoint itself was already checked.
questions.explanation: The interval may remain unchanged; use mid+1 after checking mid.

questions.title: Tower of Hanoi smallest move count
questions.description: For three pegs and n disks, the minimum number of moves is 2^n - 1. How many moves for n=3?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Compute the power first.
questions.explanation: Substitute three: eight minus one.

questions.title: Recursive digit sum
questions.description: digitSum(n) returns n when n < 10; otherwise it returns n%10 + digitSum(n/10) using integer division. What is digitSum(472)?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Remove the last digit on each call.
questions.explanation: The calls add 2, then 7, then the base digit 4.

questions.title: Choose a base result
questions.description: A recursive method counts nodes in an empty tree. What should count(null) return?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: The base case should represent the empty structure.
questions.explanation: An empty tree contains no nodes.

questions.title: Nested recursive list size
questions.description: size(n) returns 0 for null; otherwise returns 1 + size(n.next). How many nodes are counted in a chain of four nodes?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Count non-null node frames, not the null frame.
questions.explanation: Each non-null node contributes one before the null base case.

questions.title: Generate binary strings
questions.description: A recursion branches into appending 0 or 1 until length 3. How many distinct strings are generated?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: The recursion tree has 2^3 leaves.
questions.explanation: Each of three positions has two independent choices.

questions.title: Memoization effect
questions.description: A naive Fibonacci recursion recomputes many values. What does memoization change?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.

options.text: It stores computed results and reuses them
It increases the number of recursive branches

hints: Cache results by input while preserving the recursive relation.
questions.explanation: It stores answers so each subproblem is solved once, reducing repeated work.

questions.title: Recursive tree height
questions.description: A perfect binary tree has height 2 when height counts edges from root to leaf. How many levels does it contain?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Levels equal edge height plus one.
questions.explanation: Edge height two means root plus two further levels.

questions.title: Fix exponent recursion
questions.description: For power(x,n) with n>0, the simple recursive rule is x * power(x, ___), with base power(x,0)=1.
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: This version performs n recursive steps.
questions.explanation: Reduce the exponent by one for this direct recurrence.

questions.title: Fast exponentiation recurrence
questions.description: For even n, fast power computes half=power(x,n/2) then returns half*half. What is recursion depth for positive n?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Repeatedly halve until the exponent is zero.
questions.explanation: Halving n at each level gives logarithmic depth.

questions.title: Recursive subset count
questions.description: A subset generator branches into include/exclude for each of 5 distinct items. How many subsets are produced, including the empty set?
constraints: Use the stated recursive rule; assume valid inputs unless the prompt says otherwise.
hints: Count the leaves of a binary decision tree of depth five.
questions.explanation: Every item independently has two choices.
